data.insight: When a passage asks the viewer to believe a named workflow tool is operating, show the native tool surface early and direct attention to one readable node or state at a time. A polished operator form can show later human review, but labels that merely name the tool do not substitute for its native surface.
data.applies_when: A bounded real tool test supports the narrated mechanism, the native surface can be safely captured, and the viewer needs to understand a particular input, branch, output or human boundary.
data.avoid_when: The native UI is sensitive, unavailable, not the tool that performed the work, or too dense to render legibly at the delivery size. In those cases, disclose the limitation and use a different truthful proof rather than dressing a custom form up as execution evidence.

evidence.locator: Owner feedback establishing the visibility failure in r6
r6 technical pass whose scope did not establish screen legibility or native-tool visibility
